sentence: A 26-year-old man was referred to General Surgery after being accidentally diagnosed after an imaging test by the Digestive Service of a mass in the left diaphragmatic crura following admission for an IBD outbreak.
His personal history highlights: extrinsic bronchial asthma, Schonleich-Henoch purpura in childhood, ileal Crohn's disease diagnosed in 2004 and a smoker.
On physical examination, he presented abdominal pain on palpation in the right flank in relation to his IBD process and no masses or megalia were palpable.

Computed tomography (CT) identified terminal ileum with thickened walls and signs of vascular proliferation in relation to Crohn's disease, in addition to a 7.6 x 4.4 cm lesion with well-defined edges and low density with septate areas with greater enhancement. in left diaphragmatic crura.

A CT-guided percutaneous puncture was performed, the pathological result of which was reported as abundant necrotic material with numerous polymorphonucleated leukocytes and frequent histiocytes with negativity for malignant cells.

Midline laparotomy and access to the left infradiaphragmatic retroperitoneal cavity was performed with removal of the mass that was closely adhered to the adrenal gland, upper pole of the kidney and left diaphragm with excision of part of it and direct suturing of it.
The postoperative course progressed favorably, with the patient being discharged on the 7th postoperative day without immediate complications.
The final pathological report was an irregular bronchogenic cyst of elastic consistency measuring 8 x 4 x 4 cm, cavitated and purulent in appearance.
The microscopic description was reported of cystic formation with lumens lined by pseudostratified simple columnar epithelium and ciliated cells.
